title: Briefing for 2026-10-26
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-10-26: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey. UK inflation jumps to 3.5% — cementing rate hike expectations. Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes. India’s finance minister says market liquidity makes it easier for investors to exit. U.S. budget deficit swells to almost $2 trillion for fiscal 2026, up 12% in a single year. We have a $300,000 mortgage with a 2.75% interest rate. I want to pay it off. My husband says I’m crazy. Who’s right?.
global: Serbia's veteran ruler Vučić concedes election to student-led protest movement. Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election. Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile. Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates. Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban. El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages.
philippines: Lula, Brazil’s iconic working-class president, wins historic 4th term in dramatic comeback. Saudis say Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats. Carlos Yulo dethroned in world vault final, finishes 7th. 4 ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
